recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future need for explicit questionnaire designer/author metadata should be handled as a new work-group decision or extension rather than by changing FHIR-3105 retroactively.
issue_request: FHIR-3105 asked for a way to capture who designed a Questionnaire after noting that the old author concept was also used for the person who filled out an answer instance. The Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution chose publisher and contact information, removed a distinct designer concept, added Questionnaire copyright, and kept answer authorship on QuestionnaireAnswers/QuestionnaireResponse.
initial_application: The historical Jira-tagged SVN import commit 227cf05278be5788737854e9fa76bcbb663c32b3 ([3105] - Added telecom, SVN r4105) applied the issue to the old Questionnaire spreadsheet by broadening publisher wording to an organization/individual and adding Questionnaire.telecom/contact information. Later source refactors moved the active definitions into structuredefinition-Questionnaire.xml and split QuestionnaireAnswers into QuestionnaireResponse.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse. Current Questionnaire source contains publisher/contact and copyright/copyrightLabel metadata and has no active Questionnaire.author, Questionnaire.designer, Questionnaire.authority, or Questionnaire.telecom element. QuestionnaireResponse.author remains defined for the individual or device that received and recorded answers. Jira, Zulip, Confluence, and current-source searches found no later final decision that reverses the publisher/contact approach or requires a separate designer element.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because adding a new Questionnaire designer or author element would conflict with the applied resolution and the current source already preserves the intended separation between Questionnaire stewardship metadata and QuestionnaireResponse answer authorship.
